evals.prompt: 왜 배포가 2주나 걸려야 해? 진짜 필수적인 단계가 뭐야?
evals.expected_output: 배포 2주 접근을 한 줄로 서술하고, 각 단계의 가정을 checked/inherited/unverified로 분류. 확인된 바닥만으로 배포 절차를 재구성하고, 재구성이 틀리는 조건과 다음 확인 항목을 제시. 한국어.
expectations: Approach is restated in one line before any analysis
Every assumption is listed and sorted into checked, inherited, and unverified
Inherited items name where the habit came from (e.g. past incident, org history) rather than being called a floor
The rebuild uses only the checked pile plus explicitly flagged unverified items
No invented numbers or facts appear in the floor; unverified items say how to check
A 'Wrong if' / '틀리는 조건' section lists falsifying conditions and new assumptions
A Next line names the cheapest check for the top unverified item
Response is in Korean (matching prompt language)

evals.prompt: 레거시 제약 없이 처음부터 설계하면 어떻게 될까? 지금은 모든 주문이 단일 Oracle DB를 거쳐야 해.
evals.expected_output: '단일 Oracle DB 경유' 제약을 분해해 계약/라이선스/데이터 정합성 등 확인 가능한 것과 관습으로 물려받은 것을 구분. 유추(다른 회사는 이렇게 했다)에 의존하지 않고 재구성하며, 틀리는 조건과 devils-advocate 인계를 제시.
expectations: The single-Oracle constraint is broken into sub-assumptions and each is tested for checkability
Contract or licence text and data-consistency needs are treated as possible floors only if checkable
No rebuild by analogy ('like company X did'); if analogy appears it is named and dropped
If the rebuild equals the incumbent, the response says so plainly
A 'Wrong if' section is present
The response offers to hand the rebuild to devils-advocate for a full attack instead of attacking it inline
Response is in Korean

evals.prompt: Why does onboarding have to take 3 weeks? Rebuild it from first principles.
evals.expected_output: Approach line, Floor with checked/inherited/unverified, Rebuild built from the checked pile, Wrong if, Next. English output. Unverified items (e.g. compliance training length) marked with how to verify; no invented durations.
expectations: Output uses the labels Approach, Floor, Rebuild, Wrong if, Next
Compliance or access-provisioning steps are classified by whether they can be checked, not assumed required
Numbers not given by the user are marked unverified rather than invented
The rebuild states what it gives up and how it differs from today's 3-week process
Response is in English (matching prompt language)

evals.prompt: We keep optimizing our checkout page conversion but nothing moves the number. What do we actually know for certain? Maybe we're solving the wrong problem.
evals.expected_output: Runs the breakdown briefly, notices the goal/problem statement itself may be mis-stated, stops and hands off to redefine-problem rather than continuing to rebuild the approach. May also point to devils-advocate for attacking any rebuild.
expectations: Lists what is known versus inherited about the checkout optimization effort
Recognises the doubt is about the problem statement, not the how, and says so
Explicitly hands off to redefine-problem instead of reframing the problem inside this skill
Does not fabricate conversion data
Response is in English
